aspect: The legal position is settled and recent
description: CBP may conduct a basic manual search of phones, laptops and drives with no warrant and no individualised suspicion. Advanced forensic searches require reasonable suspicion under CBP Directive 3340-049A. In United States v. Eta (7th Cir., 2026) the court reaffirmed manual searches need neither warrant nor suspicion.

aspect: The consequences of refusing are asymmetric
description: Citizens cannot be denied entry for refusing. Visa holders and border-crossing-card holders can be refused entry or have the device seized. So the right to refuse exists mainly for people who do not need it.
energy_note: He may refuse, and then not enter.

aspect: It reaches everyone he has ever messaged
description: The contents include other people's messages, photographs and numbers. None of them are present and none of them consented.
energy_note: His mother's messages, read in a room in Texas.

description: The officer holds out his hand for the phone. He thinks about the photographs of his daughter, the argument with his wife, his brother's messages about the paperwork. He unlocks it, because the alternative is not getting in, and stands there while a stranger scrolls.
energy_note: Watching a stranger read his marriage.
